title: Universal flattening of a module with proper support
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Separated, finite type and proper morphisms use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Base-flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the corresponding local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $R$ be any commutative ring, let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation, and let $F$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module with support proper over $R$. There exist a scheme $T$ and a monomorphism $h:T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ of finite presentation, monomorphism meaning that for every scheme $B$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}(B,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,\operatorname{Spec}R)$ is injective, such that, for every $R$-scheme $B$, the structural morphism $B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ factors through $h$ if and only if the tensor pullback $F_B$ on $X\times_R B$ is flat over $B$. Such a factorization is unique.

proof.text: Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Finite presentation of $X\to Y$ includes quasi-separatedness; a finite presentation of an algebra on each chart in particular supplies finitely many algebra generators, so $X\to Y$ is finite type. Likewise the finite set of generators in a local finite presentation of $F$ makes $F$ finite type. Thus [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-universal-purity] applies to the proper-support carrier in the hypothesis and shows that $F$ is universally pure relative to $Y$. No flatness of $X$ or Noetherian condition on $R$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0CVI (lemma-proper-pure), clause (1); the finite type implications are immediate from the finite presentations

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-pure-dimension-flatness-representability] with this $X\to Y$, this $F$, and $n=0$. Its finite presentation hypotheses are precisely those of the item, and its universal purity hypothesis is step 1. It gives an algebraic space $E_0$, a finite-presentation monomorphism $j_0:E_0\to Y$, and the bijection on scheme tests onto the maps satisfying $P_0$.

For any $R$-scheme $B$, in the explicit chart condition $P_0$ the inequality $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(u)\geq0$ holds for every point: transcendence degree is a supremum of cardinalities, and the empty independent set has cardinality zero [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Thus $P_0(B\to Y)$ requires flatness at every stalk on every etale scheme chart, exactly the definition of $F_B$ being flat over $B$. Conversely that flatness implies every stalk condition in $P_0$. The tensor pullback and projection are the same in both conditions.

The finite-presentation morphism $j_0$ is locally of finite type, since its chart algebras of finite presentation are in particular finitely generated. It is also a monomorphism on all scheme tests by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-space-lft-monomorphism-separated-lqf] to $E_0\to h_Y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. This gives exactly chartwise local quasi-finiteness and the closed-immersion diagonal required by [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable]. The latter gives a scheme $T$ and an isomorphism $h_T\simeq E_0$ over $Y$. Let $h:T\to Y$ be the composite represented by $h_T\simeq E_0\to h_Y$.

source.place: Schemehood step in Tag 0CXB (theorem-existence); spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 0463 (lemma-monomorphism-loc-finite-type-loc-quasi-finite) and 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme)

proof.text: The isomorphism $h_T\simeq E_0$ identifies scheme charts, the point topologies, and the relative diagonals, so the quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and chartwise local finite presentation of $j_0$ give finite presentation of $h$. Explicitly a chart into either source is carried to a chart into the other with the identical scheme domain and identical map to $Y$; the same holds for charts of the relative diagonals. For any scheme $B$, the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(B,T)\simeq E_0(B)$ commutes with the maps to $\operatorname{Hom}(B,Y)$. It makes this map injective, and its image is exactly the maps satisfying $P_0$, hence by step 3 exactly the maps with flat $F_B$. Existence of a factorization is membership in this image, and injectivity gives uniqueness. This proves every asserted clause.

lean.statement: theorem exists_universalFlattening_of_properSupport (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from (Spec R)))) (hsep : MapIsSeparated f) (hfp : ProperQuotFinitePresentation f) (F : X.QCoh) (hF : F.obj.IsFinitePresentation) (hsupp : ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom ∧ MapIsProper (i ≫ f) ∧ ∃ G : Z.Modules, G.IsQuasicoherent ∧ G.IsFiniteType ∧ Nonempty ((moduleDirectImage i).obj G ≅ F.obj)) : ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ Spec R), LocallyOfFinitePresentation h ∧ QuasiCompact h ∧ QuasiSeparated h ∧ (∀ B : Scheme.{u}, Function.Injective (fun g : B ⟶ T ↦ g ≫ h)) ∧ ∀ B : ProperQuotTest (schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from (Spec R)))), (∃! g : B.left.left ⟶ T, g ≫ h = (yoneda.preimage B.hom).left) ↔ ∀ U : (properQuotFibre f B).EtaleSite, ((schemeRestriction (properQuotFibre f B) U).obj ((moduleTensorPullback (properQuotFst f B)).obj F.obj)).IsFlatOver (yoneda.preimage (U.obj.hom ≫ (properQuotSnd f B).hom.hom)).left
